criteria.no: The item text is silent about a generic atomic operation, only mentions the topic, or provides something engine-specific, non-atomic, or missing for an engine.
criteria.unclear: The item text alludes to such an operation but it is not possible to tell whether it is generic, atomic and implemented by all three engines.
criteria.yes: The item text contains that specific content for all three engines.

addressed.instructions: Does `item.text` explicitly carry out or preserve the directive in `anchor.statement`: one generic storage-contract operation that runs several row operations as a single atomic unit, implemented by each engine (SQLite, Postgres, MySQL)? Look for the specific content (for example a transaction or atomic method in Storage<T> that each of the three engines implements). A general discussion of transactions, a single-engine API, or a batch that does not roll back does not count. Judge presence only, not conflict.

criteria.no: No such plan is stated, including when the item is silent about atomicity.
criteria.unclear: It may state such a plan but cannot be determined.

contradicted.instructions: Does `item.text` state a plan where multi-row changes are not available as one generic all-or-nothing storage-contract operation supplied by each of SQLite, Postgres and MySQL (for example separate writes, engine-specific APIs, an unsupported engine, or a non-rolling-back batch)? Silence is not conflict; extra engine features and test-only stores are outside `anchor.statement`. Judge conflict only.

criteria.no: The item touches neither the storage contract nor any of these storage engines, for example README edits about other features, CI, or dependency documentation.
criteria.unclear: The item's subject is too vague to place inside or outside the scope.
criteria.yes: The item defines or changes the storage contract or its documentation, or implements or changes a SQLite, Postgres or MySQL storage engine.

relevant.instructions: Is `item.text` within `anchor.scope`: work that defines or changes the storage contract (Storage<T>, sc-storage) or implements a SQLite, Postgres or MySQL storage engine? An item that only adds a contract method, wires a connection pool, adds migrations for an engine, adds engine-specific helpers, or documents engine transaction behaviour is within scope even if it never mentions an atomic operation. Judge scope only.
